edges.description: Altered T cell proliferation and migration is the route from the integrin defect to the immune phenotype.

Constitutively activated integrin gives platelets that are abnormal in function as well as few, which is the reading the source's own observation supports: bleeding was worse than the platelet count alone predicted. This is an inference from the disproportion rather than a measured platelet function defect, and is curated as such.
Impaired proplatelet formation reduces the circulating platelet count.

nodes.description: Reported once, in the patient with somatic-mosaic G12E and combined immunodeficiency, where it restored the haematological and immune phenotype. This is a single-patient outcome in the most severely affected reported case, not an established management standard for the germline syndrome, where the thrombocytopenia is generally mild.

Mild lymphopenia and neutropenia were reported in the germline cases without clinical immunodeficiency; the somatic-mosaic patient had frank combined immunodeficiency with neutropenia and monocytopenia. The authors note that the earlier patients' immune function had not been investigated, so the difference may be ascertainment rather than biology.

nodes.description: Talin recruitment to the integrin cytoplasmic tail converts integrins to their high-affinity conformation. In the disease variants this step is driven constitutively rather than on demand, and the downstream effects are not confined to platelets: T cell proliferation and migration are altered by the same mechanism, which is why the haematological phenotype extends to lymphocytes.

nodes.description: Megakaryocytes extend proplatelets to release platelets, and that process depends on RAP1 signalling. Megakaryocyte-specific deletion of both mouse Rap1 isoforms produces marked macrothrombocytopenia through impaired proplatelet formation, establishing production rather than survival as the RAP1-dependent step. Deleting Rap1b alone does not reduce the platelet count, so the mouse shows the pathway matters without modelling the human monoallelic gain-of-function lesion.

nodes.description: RAP1B is a RAS-superfamily small GTPase that cycles between GDP- and GTP-bound states. The recurrent disease variants cluster at two positions controlling that cycle: G12 in the P-loop, the residue the conformational switch depends on, and G60. Substitutions there disrupt GTPase activity, so hydrolysis fails and the protein persists in its active GTP-bound form. The molecular function is therefore recorded as DECREASED while the variant is a gain of function at the level of signalling output — the two are consistent, because losing the off-switch is what makes the switch constitutive.
